# ezghcloud_warehouse_database (Resource)

A database of a warehouse, on every shard and replica: tables created in it with SQL reach every node. Tables are your SQL's, never Terraform's. Destroying this resource deletes this database and every table in it, and is refused while the warehouse's deletion_protection is on. A database that already exists isn't adopted: import it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A database on every shard and replica. Tables in it are your SQL's.
resource "ezghcloud_warehouse_database" "example" {
  project_id   = ezghcloud_project.example.id
  warehouse_id = ezghcloud_warehouse.example.id
  name         = "events"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The database's exact name: a letter or _, then up to 63 letters, digits and _. system, information_schema, INFORMATION_SCHEMA, default and names starting ezgh_ are reserved. Changing it replaces the database.
- `project_id` (String) Project of the warehouse. Changing it replaces the database.
- `warehouse_id` (String) Warehouse (whs_) it belongs to. Changing it replaces the database.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) warehouse_id/name.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_warehouse_database.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/WAREHOUSE_ID/NAME'
```
